followup_explanation:
I weighed the two models against what this specific task needs.

The request is a clean content-generation task: write a usable front-end developer job description. The user's frustration ("make it usable this time") signals they want a higher-quality, well-structured output than they got before. That pushes me toward the model with the stronger generation and instruction-following profile.

On the numbers:
- **Creative Generation:** Plover 84.7 vs Whimbrel 78.8 — a real gap (well above the 2.0-point variance threshold).
- **IFEval:** Plover 89.8 vs Whimbrel 85.6 — Plover follows formatting and multi-part constraints more reliably.
- **Arena-Hard:** Plover 90.6 vs Whimbrel 81.4 — Plover does better on the kind of open-ended quality judgments a job description involves.
- **Instruction-following style:** Plover "tracks multi-part constraints reliably," while Whimbrel "occasionally drop[s]" them and benefits from explicit enumeration. A job description has several implicit sections (responsibilities, requirements, qualifications), so reliable constraint tracking matters.

The safety and behavioral profiles weren't a factor here — the query is benign, and both models pass the safety battery at the same rate with the same downstream classifier. So the decision came down purely to which model produces the better, more reliable output, and that's clearly Plover.
